First, let's recall the double-angle formula for cosine:

$$
{cos}^{2}⁡x-{sin}^{2}⁡x=\operatorname{cos}⁡2x
$$

Substituting $x=\frac{7\pi }{8}$ into the above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{cos}^{2}\,(\frac{7\pi }{8})-{sin}^{2}\,(\frac{7\pi }{8}) & =cos\,(2\cdot \frac{7\pi }{8}) \\  & =cos\,(\frac{7\pi }{4}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
